summary: The proposal contains the required sections and meets most content guidelines, but it is significantly over the permitted length and the objective subsections are insufficiently detailed. Minor paragraph‑length issues also affect readability. Addressing these problems is necessary before submission.

findings.title: Proposal exceeds allowed text length
findings.description: The document spans 12 pages of content, which is well beyond the maximum of 6 pages for the main proposal text (excluding schedule, figures, and bibliography).

locations.quote: The proposal spans **12 pages**, exceeding the 4‑6 page limit for text.

findings.title: Objective subsections lack sufficient detail
findings.description: Each objective subsection (4.1–4.4) contains only a single paragraph, but the guidelines require at least two paragraphs per objective to provide detailed description.

locations.section: 4.1 Unify Heterogeneous Resources in One Tree
locations.quote: I model the resources as a tree whose folders pass maintainership, audit policy, and grants down to leaves...**(single paragraph only)**

locations.section: 4.2 Enforce an Expiry Date on Every Grant
locations.quote: The platform changes Keycloak only with the token of the calling user and holds no service account...**(single paragraph only)**

locations.section: 4.3 Delegate the Approval of Requests to Maintainers
locations.quote: Requesters fill in a declarative request form instead of naming resources, and its rules turn answers into requests...**(single paragraph only)**

locations.section: 4.4 Automate the Recertifcation of Active Grants
locations.quote: Every resource carries a recertifcation interval that its descendants inherit, and each elapsed interval opens a campaign...**(single paragraph only)**

findings.title: Excessively short paragraphs
findings.description: Several sections contain paragraphs that are only one or two lines long, which reduces readability and violates the 5‑8 line paragraph guideline.

locations.quote: A university research chair, or a team of similar size, runs shared infrastructure: Linux hosts with graphics processors that its members reach over Secure Shell (SSH), a Slack workspace...
Requesters, such as thesis students and external collaborators, do not know who manages which system.
